+slug: pagerduty
+name: PagerDuty
+category: Observability
+description: Work with PagerDuty incidents, services, schedules and on-calls, with your key.
+enabled: true
+adapter: api_key
+auth:
+  type: api_key
+  refresh: none
+  api_key:
+    fields:
+      - name: api_key
+        label: API key
+        secret: true
+        help: User Settings, Create API User Token. A user token acts as you, with your access.
+      - name: region
+        label: Service region
+        secret: false
+        help: The region your PagerDuty account is in.
+        choices:
+          - pagerduty.com
+          - eu.pagerduty.com
+    # Checks the key against the REST API's current user, which a user API
+    # token can read; the hosted MCP server does not support dynamic client
+    # registration, so a key is the simplest shape here.
+    identity:
+      method: GET
+      url: "https://api.{region}/users/me"
+      headers:
+        Authorization: "Token token={api_key}"
+      account_id: user.id
+      label: user.email
+    help_url: https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/api-access-keys
+# A key does not expire, and only PagerDuty can revoke it, so it is never
+# handed to an agent: whatever runs beside the agent could keep it for good.
+token: { kind: pass_through, max_lifetime: null }
+mcp:
+  servers:
+    # The PagerDuty-hosted MCP server takes a user API key in an
+    # Authorization: Token token=<key> header. EU accounts use mcp.eu.
+    - name: pagerduty
+      url: "https://mcp.{region}/mcp"
+      headers:
+        Authorization: "Token token={api_key}"
+tools: { mode: pass_through }

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+---
+name: pagerduty
+description: Work with PagerDuty incidents, services, schedules and on-calls through its MCP tools, acting with the owner's PagerDuty access.
+---
+
+# PagerDuty
+
+The `pagerduty` MCP server gives you PagerDuty's own tools for incidents,
+services, schedules, on-calls, teams and escalation policies. You act as the
+owner of this connection, with whatever their PagerDuty access allows.
+
+How to work with it:
+
+- Start by reading. Find the incident, service or schedule and look at its
+  current state before you change anything. Quote what you found: the incident
+  or service, and a link to the PagerDuty page, so a person can check it.
+- During an incident, on-call people are under pressure. Keep notes and updates
+  short and factual, and say which incident they belong to.
+- Change incidents, services, schedules or overrides only when you were asked
+  to, and say what you changed. Paging someone, reassigning an incident or
+  editing a schedule affects real people's night, so confirm the target before
+  you act.
+- Production and on-call data can include personal information. Summarise
+  rather than copying raw details into rooms, and never post secrets.
+
+If a tool answers that the request is not allowed, the connection's access does
+not cover it (some actions and filters need a user-level key): say so rather
+than trying another way.

+def test_the_shipped_pagerduty_entry_pastes_a_key_and_picks_a_region():
+    definition = CATALOG["pagerduty"].definition
+    assert definition.adapter == "api_key"
+    sign_in = definition.auth.api_key
+    assert sign_in is not None
+    assert [(f.name, f.secret) for f in sign_in.fields] == [
+        ("api_key", True),
+        ("region", False),
+    ]
+    assert sign_in.choice_names() == {"region"}
+    # PagerDuty's hosted MCP server takes the key in Authorization: Token
+    # token=<key>; EU accounts live under mcp.eu.
+    assert definition.mcp is not None
+    [server] = definition.mcp.servers
+    assert server.url == "https://mcp.{region}/mcp"
+    assert server.headers == {"Authorization": "Token token={api_key}"}
+    assert sign_in.identity.method == "GET"
+    assert sign_in.identity.url == "https://api.{region}/users/me"
+    assert (sign_in.identity.account_id, sign_in.identity.label) == (
+        "user.id",
+        "user.email",
+    )
+    # A key never expires, so it is never handed to an agent.
+    assert definition.token is not None
+    assert definition.token.max_lifetime is None
+
+
